steps: Implement datasets and their refresh pipelines with retention enforcement (packages/data/migrations/datasets).
Implement entity resolution producing link proposals with evidence.
Implement outputs as reviewed imports into each module's use cases.
Court and debt datasets are off by default in every hub and need an impact assessment to enable (ADR 012).
acceptance: Court and debt records about natural persons are never displayed (tested).
No dataset output reaches reputation.
People are linked only with their own confirmation; personal-data datasets cannot activate without a recorded legal basis.

packages.title: AI provenance and labelling for text, translations and images
packages.goal: Record and show how AI contributed to every publication, translation and image: reader-visible labels naming the responsible human, C2PA manifests and IPTC digital source types on generated images.
steps: Define a provenance record contract (none, ai_assisted, machine_translated_reviewed, generated) with the responsible person.
Add label strings in every engine language and render them on publications, translations and images.
Behind an adapter with a fake, attach C2PA manifests with IPTC digitalSourceType to generated or AI-edited images.
acceptance: No AI-assisted content renders without a label (tested).
A machine translation stays a draft until a named reviewer approves it.
Generated images carry trainedAlgorithmicMedia or compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia.

packages.title: Autonomous editorial office with story clusters
packages.goal: Discover and propose sources with recorded legal checks, ingest, deduplicate, cluster stories with multi-source attribution, draft, translate, check facts and similarity, label AI images and fill review queues; people approve every publication.
steps: Implement discovery and legal checks (robots, terms digest, licence) producing proposals.
Implement ingestion for RSS, Atom, sitemaps and APIs; page crawling only for sources whose checks permit it.
Implement deduplication and story clusters that reference, never copy, source items and list every source with time and link.

Implement drafting, translation, similarity and fact-check steps behind model routes; display-only sources are excluded from drafting; the review workbench API, calendar and magazine assembly proposals.
acceptance: No code path publishes without a person's approval (tested).
A source whose robots or terms change is paused automatically.
Every cluster lists all member sources; AI images carry reader and metadata labels.

packages.title: Manufacturer and supplier knowledge pages: products, guides, training and events
packages.goal: Within the hub's legal basis and each source's licence and robots rules, build sourced manufacturer and supplier pages and index their products, installation guides, data sheets, warranty conditions, training, technical articles and events (ADR 010 decision 19).
steps: Add product_entry and learning_resource (packages/data/migrations/manufacturers); tag items with plan-step keys and ETIM classes where licensed.
Crawl only logged-off public pages through sources whose crawl policy allows it, honouring robots.txt and RSL; store facts and links, not full documents, unless licensed; record per-field provenance.
Keep sourced labels until the company claims its page (CLM-001); let claimed manufacturers supply catalogues, guides and training under an explicit licence.
Takedown requests remove the item and propagate tombstones.
Offer claimed manufacturers a free structured knowledge feed and only aggregate signals (cohorts of at least ten), never who read or specified their products.
acceptance: No content is collected behind a login or technical barrier (collector configuration test).
A robots or terms change pauses the pipeline until reviewed.
Sourced product entries cannot be quoted or ordered until the company publishes an offering.
No manufacturer view shows an individual reader or specifier (negative test).

packages.title: Plan-step recommendations with explanations, never paid
packages.goal: For every plan step recommend relevant materials and products, articles and guides, training and courses, events, consultants and contacts, each with an explanation of why it fits; sponsored content, where a hub allows it, is labelled and kept out of ranking.
steps: Add recommendation_method_version, recommendation_set, recommendation and sponsored_placement (packages/data/migrations/recommendations).

Match plan items to targets through the shared plan-step taxonomy and structured attributes; semantic recall is added once RAG-301 is done; courses and events come from LRN-001 and EVT-001 when those modules are enabled.
Explain every recommendation (matched step terms, unknowns, source label); sourced items stay labelled sourced until claimed.
Show sponsored placements only in a separate labelled slot.
acceptance: Recommendation ranks are identical with and without sponsored placements, entitlements and commissions (test).
Every recommendation names the matched step terms and the unknowns.
Private plan data never leaves the owner's projection when computing recommendations.

packages.title: Planner templates and marketplace category rules (hub administration)
packages.goal: Hub experts maintain plan templates per country and project type; operators set marketplace category rules (who may offer, verification, refunds, agent automation) that reference the commission versions of BILL-003.
steps: Implement plan template versions with author and reviewer separation (packages/data/migrations/planner-admin).
Implement marketplace category rules and refund windows; commissions are BILL-003 versions.
Expose both through the admin facade with audit.
acceptance: A template author cannot publish their own template (tested).
Licensed categories accept only providers with a checked licence.
No category rule changes ranking or matching.

packages.title: Public-register and licence-board facts as sourced records
packages.goal: Display licence status from state boards, business-entity status, SAM.gov registration and exclusion status, OSHA inspections and LEI (and official ratings in other countries) with source, observed time, licence and link, never blended into reputation.
steps: Define a sourced-fact contract: subject, fact kind, value, source id, licence flags, observed_at, valid_until, link.

Add register-fact adapters with deterministic fakes for one US licence-board file, SAM.gov entity status, DOL OSHA inspections and GLEIF LEI; live mode off by default and behind second-person activation.
Link facts to companies only through identifiers from the pack, never by name alone.
Render sourced facts with a distinct treatment and a "how this is sourced" explanation in every locale.
Keep a register adapters catalogue per country pack (access method, licence, refresh cadence) and an expiry watch that reminds the subject before a licence or registration lapses.
acceptance: Sourced facts never change a reputation snapshot (comparison test).
A fact without a licence flag permitting display is not shown; expired facts are labelled stale.
Wording never claims "certified" or "licensed by Trustwork".
Expiring facts trigger a reminder to the subject before the expiry date (clock test).

packages.title: Prequalification passport shared by consent
packages.goal: Let a company keep one prequalification passport (licences, insurance certificates with expiry reminders, bonding capacity, safety record, references, financial summary) and share a chosen subset with a client by consent for a limited time, free for subcontractors.
steps: Define passport sections with sourced, claimed and verified status per item and expiry.
Collect insurance certificates as claimed documents; confirm them with the issuer where the hub configures a recipe; remind before expiry.
Share by consent grants with scope, recipient and expiry; revocation stops access immediately.

Map passport sections to national question sets and statutory partner checks from country packs (for example the UK Common Assessment Standard and Finland's contractor obligations) so one passport answers many clients.
acceptance: A client sees only the sections granted, only until expiry (negative tests).
Self-declared items are labelled claimed until a document is reviewed.
Subcontractors are never charged to hold or share a passport.
A client in a country with a statutory partner-check list sees which required items are present, missing or expired.

packages.title: Building permits and inspections as sourced project data
packages.goal: Import municipal permit records where open-data terms allow (or through a licensed aggregator adapter) as sourced facts linked to contractors and to a person's own plan, with inspection reminders for one's own projects.
steps: Define permit and inspection fact contracts with source, licence and jurisdiction.
Implement one open-data adapter and one aggregator port with fakes.
Link permits to companies by licence number only; never publish homeowner names or private addresses; let a plan step track its permit and inspection dates.
acceptance: Public views contain no homeowner names (negative test).
Facts carry jurisdiction, source and observed time.
Sources without reuse rights are rejected at configuration.

packages.title: Integrations: public API, webhooks, CSV import, calendars and accounting adapters
packages.goal: Let participants and hubs connect Trustwork to their tools: a documented public API over the public projection and one's own data with OAuth, signed webhooks, calendar feeds, CSV import of one's own contacts and projects, and accounting and project-tool adapters with fakes.
steps: Publish API scopes that map to projections; issue OAuth clients per participant and per hub.
Implement signed webhooks with replay protection and per-subscriber delivery logs.
Import CSV as the importer's private contacts or projects; never create directory members or claims.
Add accounting and project-tool adapters with fakes; meter and show external API usage costs to the hub.
acceptance: API tokens never read beyond their projection scopes (negative tests).
CSV import never creates a public company or person record (test).
Webhook signatures verify and replays are rejected.

packages.title: Backup, restore drill and retention automation
packages.goal: Turn the runbook's restore drill into scripts and evidence on synthetic data.
steps: Script base backups and WAL archiving for the compose stack with encrypted off-host targets as configuration.
Script a point-in-time restore into an isolated network with providers disabled.
Replay erasure tombstones recorded after the backup and reconcile queued jobs without re-sending effects.
Implement audit and outbox partition retention per configuration.
acceptance: A recorded drill on synthetic data restores, replays erasures and measures recovery time and data-loss window.
Restored workers do not contact providers before reconciliation.

packages.title: Backups, restore drills, updates and health in the console backend
packages.goal: Scheduled encrypted backups, restore drills with evidence, two-person restore and production migrations, update notices, readiness and health counts for the console.
steps: Implement backup records and drills against an isolated environment.
Implement update checks and migration status with backup-before-apply.
Implement readiness and health aggregates for the console.
acceptance: A restore replays tombstones before reconnecting workers.
A production migration without a fresh backup is refused (tested).
Restore and production migration need two people.

packages.title: One-command installation with Docker Compose and the setup token
packages.goal: Let anyone start a node with one command: PostgreSQL, S3-compatible object storage, migrations, API, web and worker, printing a one-time setup URL.
steps: Write infra/install/compose.yaml on top of the OPS-002 images with healthchecks, a one-shot migrate service and distinct owner and runtime database roles.
Generate secrets locally on first start; never commit or print them except the one-time setup token.
Write Railway, Fly.io and Kubernetes guides as tested recipes or label them untested; no deployment by this package.
Smoke test: a fresh install reaches the setup wizard.
acceptance: docker compose up on a clean machine reaches /admin/setup with a valid token.
No default password survives first start.
Upgrades run migrations forward only after a backup.

packages.title: Hub console shell, overview, approvals, setup wizard and hub settings on fixtures (console M1)
packages.goal: Build the console shell and its first milestone fixtures-first: AdminShell, permission-filtered navigation, elevation gate, overview, approvals, help, setup wizard, hub identity, modes, modules, legal, residency, country base, taxonomy and launch checklist (supersedes the earlier /admin MVP surface).
steps: Build fixtures validated by the contract schemas for the US demo hub and the Samarkand example hub, and staff personas including staff-none.
Build the shell, the data port and the M1 screens with every state; section-local fixtures live in each section folder so later slices do not edit shared files.
Strings in an admin locale namespace for every engine language; Playwright and axe at 1280, 768 and 375 px.
acceptance: Denied state on every route for staff-none.
No English text in non-English locales; a demo band is visible on demo data.
No hub switcher in the header; every page names the one hub it acts on.

packages.title: Console M2: keys, models and automation screens on fixtures
packages.goal: Build the providers, secret field, connection tests, routing, egress, budgets, usage and kill-switch screens and the schedules, runs and alerts screens on fixtures.
steps: Build the integrations section with the write-only SecretField, ConnectionTestPanel, RoutingTable, EgressMatrix and KillSwitchControl.
Build the automation section with CronField, run tables and logs.
Locale namespace for every engine language; Playwright and axe.
acceptance: A DOM scan finds no secret value.
The egress matrix is operable by keyboard and screen reader.
Kill-switch release shows the two-person requirement.

packages.title: Console M3: editorial office and data screens on fixtures
packages.goal: Build the editorial sections (sources, discovery, pipelines, review workbench, calendar, publications, magazine, translations, policy) and the data sections (datasets, batches, links, knowledge, recommendations) on fixtures.
steps: Build the editorial sections including the review workbench with sources beside the draft.
Build datasets, batches, links, knowledge and recommendations, including the sponsored-content policy (off by default).
Locale namespace for every engine language; Playwright and axe.
acceptance: No publish control exists outside the review decision.
No merge control exists anywhere; link proposals offer only accept or reject.
AI labels are visible.

packages.title: Console M4: participants, support and trust screens on fixtures
packages.goal: Build people, companies, claims, verification, credentials and consents, the support workspace and the trust sections (moderation, disputes, reputation methods, appeals, screening, confirmations) on fixtures.
steps: Build participants and support sections.
Build trust and safety sections.
Locale namespace for every engine language; Playwright and axe.
acceptance: No impersonation route or control (scan).
No control sets a score or badge (scan).
The case-grant journey works with a second approver.

packages.title: Console M5: modules, agents, extensions and billing screens on fixtures
packages.goal: Build module sections (projects, planner, marketplace, shared knowledge, events, learning, matching, commerce), the agent product sections including jurisdiction agent settings and the governed extension registry, the billing sections and communications on fixtures.
steps: Build module sections including planner templates, marketplace rules and shared knowledge review.

Build agent modules, policy (with per-jurisdiction disclosure, liability and limits from HUB-005), external agents, usage, abuse and the extension registry (declared actions, inputs, data classes, side effects, endpoints, costs, mandate kinds, safety-suite result, second-person activation).
Build billing (offers, prices with cost beside sale price, commissions, invoices, payouts, credits, tax) and communications sections; locale namespace; Playwright and axe.
acceptance: Cohort counts under ten are rendered as suppressed.
Price, commission and extension activation need a second person.
No screen lists or manages individual participants' agents.

packages.title: Console M6: federation, privacy, staff, audit, operations and node console on fixtures
packages.goal: Build the remaining hub sections and the node console on fixtures.
steps: Build federation, privacy, staff and audit, and operations sections.
Build the node console (hubs, node staff, updates, backups, identity and keys, kill switches, read-only restricted places).
Locale namespace for every engine language; Playwright and axe.
acceptance: Restore and production migration need two people.
The locale completeness screen blocks activation of incomplete templates.
The restricted-places list is read-only.

packages.title: Console live wiring: shell, setup, hub settings, approvals and staff
packages.goal: Replace the fixture adapter with the API for the core sections as their backends land.
steps: Implement the API adapter of the console data port for hub, setup, approvals and staff use cases.
Run the M1 browser plan against the API with negative authorization.
acceptance: Every private object is not found to staff without a case grant through these paths (tested).
Setup completes against the API with a second factor.

packages.title: Console live wiring: keys, models, automation, editorial and data
packages.goal: Wire the M2 and M3 sections to the API.
steps: Implement the API adapter methods for providers, routes, egress, budgets, kill switches, pipelines, runs, editorial items, sources, datasets and links.
Run the M2 and M3 browser plans against the API.
acceptance: A DOM and network scan finds no secret value.
Publishing still needs the review decision against the live API.

packages.title: Console live wiring: participants, support, trust, modules, agents and billing
packages.goal: Wire the M4 and M5 sections to the API.
steps: Implement the API adapter methods for participants, claims, support, trust, modules, agent product, extensions and billing.
Run the M4 and M5 browser plans against the API with negative authorization.
acceptance: No impersonation path exists against the API (scan and test).
Extension activation needs a passing safety suite and a second person against the API.

packages.title: Console live wiring: federation, privacy, operations and node console
packages.goal: Wire the M6 sections and the node console to the API.
steps: Implement the API adapter methods for federation peers, privacy requests, staff, audit, operations and node console.
Run the M6 browser plan against the API.
acceptance: Erasure execution and restore need two people against the API (tested).
Raising a peering level above syndicate needs a second approver.

packages.title: Hub operator console (umbrella): end-to-end acceptance of every section
packages.goal: Umbrella for the console packages (HUBC-000, ADM-002, HUBC-002 to HUBC-010): the console is complete when every section described in the handbook works against the API with the guard rails proven end to end.
steps: Run the full console browser plan against the API at three widths in every hub language of the US demo hub (en, es) and one other example hub.
Run the guard-rail scans: no ranking control, no impersonation, no secret rendering, no private object without a case grant.
Record limitations and remaining gaps per section in docs/quality/release/hub-console.md.
acceptance: Every private object returns not found to staff without a case grant, through every console path.
Activating a legal document without counsel approval fails.
No console control sets a score, position or badge directly.

packages.title: Durable mandate and action workflow with fakes
packages.goal: Deliver structured runs, actions, approvals and reconciliation without live paid providers.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/assistant: mandate, mandate_context, mandate_revision, run, run_step, action_intent, action_attempt, action_outcome, approval, reconciliation, service_backlog_item, conversation_turn and assistant_note.
Define the mandate and action digest and the current-right recheck; persist operation and attempt identity before dispatch, with outbox, reservations and fencing.
Implement fake model, channel, order and payment ports and stateful reconciliation; use the retrieval port with a fake until RAG-301 (RAG-401 verifies the integration).
Exercise cancellation, revocation, asynchronous receipts and crash recovery.
acceptance: A crash after an external effect and before the result is saved leads to reconciliation by a second worker, not a blind replay (tested).
Acknowledged or pending is not final success; an accepted-then-rejected outcome is tested.
An unknown outcome retains reservations until a definitive result; private constraints never leak.
Prompt text cannot alter mandates.

packages.title: Freeze agent catalogue contracts: mandate v2, modules, metering, goals, envelopes, connections
packages.goal: Add the catalogue schemas as a new contract file without changing the frozen v1 shapes, so backend, billing and web work can proceed independently.
steps: Add MandateV2 (action vocabulary v2, context selectors, structured conditions, approval policies, approver rules, escalation, grantee) keeping MandateSchema as the v1 subset.
Add module manifest, hub agent policy, agent plan version, meter rate version and usage record schemas.
Add goal, trigger, job subscription, agent envelope (with the new intents) and report schemas.
Add external connection, connection token, connection call and kill switch schemas; generate JSON Schema and validated examples.
acceptance: confirm_execution can never be pre-authorized by any schema-valid mandate (tested).
A note-kind condition forces ask-each in the pure policy function.
Forbidden-field tests cover budget ranges, constraint records, private data classes and token hashes in every non-owner projection.
Frozen v1 fixtures still validate unchanged.

packages.title: Agent goals, agent-to-agent envelopes, negotiation sessions, company mandates and the company representative
packages.goal: Let a participant direct their single agent with goals, let a company keep one standing representative with an accountable person, and let agents of different participants negotiate safely through structured objects.
steps: Model goal, goal progress, job subscription, agent report, agent envelope, negotiation session, company representative and company mandate (packages/data/migrations/agents).
Implement goal creation that proposes the missing mandate changes in one structured confirmation; envelope delivery with intents, digests of referenced versions and untrusted note handling.
Implement negotiation sessions with round limits, expiry and escalation to humans.

Implement the company representative (one per company, accountable person, re-confirmation within 7 days after the granting member leaves, automatic suspension, labels, company budgets only) and hub- and node-level kill switches for agent dispatch.
acceptance: No envelope note can change state; only structured intents after receiver mandate checks (tested).
Private constraints never appear in envelopes, shared threads or logs visible to counterparties; competing sellers never receive each other's pricing.
Revoking membership stops dependent company mandates in the same transaction.
Exactly one assistant surface per person and at most one representative per company; no agent management UI.

packages.title: Agent module registry, hub agent policy, job subscriptions and kill switches
packages.goal: Let a hub enable and configure engine modules, let a principal turn jobs on through mandate proposals, and stop dispatch at every kill-switch level.
steps: Load module manifests shipped with the engine and the activated extension versions of AGT-023; reject hub settings that widen actions, tools or data classes beyond the manifest.
Store the hub agent policy as the agents domain of hub_config_version with second-person activation; module eligibility (persons, company members, representative, verified companies only).
Implement job subscriptions with schedule, event, deadline, goal and request triggers in the principal's time zone and hub calendar.
Implement node, hub, hub module, hub connections, company representative, person and connection kill switches through authorization epochs.
acceptance: Turning a job on creates only a mandate proposal; nothing runs until it is confirmed on the first-party form (tested).
Each kill switch blocks the next action check; executing actions go to reconciliation.
No module code path branches on a country code (lint or test).

packages.title: Agent metering, quotas, agent plans and usage statistics
packages.goal: Meter agent usage idempotently, enforce quotas and protection limits, let a hub price modules with versioned, second-person-activated records and see cohort statistics.
steps: Append usage records idempotently per run step, attempt and meter.
Check quota windows per principal, module and meter; reserve estimates from the named platform budget beyond the included quota and settle on actuals.
Implement agent plan versions and metered price versions (cost beside sale price) on offers, price versions and acceptances; protection limits stay independent of plans.
Cohort usage statistics with every count under ten suppressed; abuse signals open cases for staff.
acceptance: Replaying a step never charges twice; unknown billing outcomes reconcile.
Without a platform budget a job stops at quota and asks.
Introduction quotas, alert timing and ranking are identical with and without paid entitlements (tests).

packages.title: Detailed agent settings for every participant, with previews and explanations
packages.goal: Let participants configure their own agent in detail (ADR 010 decision 22): goals, modules, behaviour and tone, mandates and limits per action, budgets, schedules, channels, approval rules, what to share with whom, and external connections, with a preview and an explanation of every setting.
steps: Contracts for an agent settings document per person (and per company representative) that compiles into existing objects: mandate proposals, job subscriptions, approval rules, channel grants, sharing rules and connection scopes; settings never authorize by themselves.
Implement a dry-run preview: given the settings, list what the agent would do this week, which actions need approval and which jurisdiction limits (HUB-005) apply, with plain-language explanations.
Validate every setting against the hub agent policy and jurisdiction limits; explain refusals.
Version settings with history and one-click revert; export one's own settings.
acceptance: Saving settings never widens authority without the structured mandate confirmation (tested).
The preview matches what the runtime then does in a deterministic test.
Every setting has an explanation string in every engine language.

packages.title: Governed extension registry for agent capabilities
packages.goal: Let hub administrators add functions, tools, integrations and capabilities to agents through a governed registry (ADR 010 decision 22) without ever bypassing mandates, budgets, kill switches, privacy rules, the restricted-places list or the untrusted-text rule.
steps: Contracts for an extension manifest: declared actions (mapped to mandate kinds), inputs, data classes read and sent, side effects, external endpoints, cost model, required mandate kinds, adapter and fake, and the safety-suite reference.

Registry lifecycle draft, tested, active, suspended and retired: an extension activates only after its safety suite passed on the fake adapter (EVAL-001 harness) and a second person approved it; activation is a hub configuration version.

Runtime enforcement: extension actions go through the same mandate, budget, approval, egress (KEYS-001) and kill-switch checks as built-in actions; endpoints in restricted places are refused; untrusted outputs never issue commands.
Audit every extension call by digest; suspend an extension automatically when its safety suite fails after an engine update.
acceptance: An extension that declares an action without a mandate kind is rejected (tested).
An extension call outside a valid mandate or above a budget is refused like a built-in action (negative tests).
An endpoint in a restricted place cannot be registered.
Activation by the drafter alone fails.

packages.title: Model gateway with egress-policy routing and per-mandate cost caps
packages.goal: Provide one model port that routes every call by data class and hub egress policy, reserves cost from the platform budget per mandate and run, and logs metadata without bodies.
steps: Define the gateway contract: data class, allowed connections, retention requirement, residency, cost estimate, reservation id.
Implement a deterministic fake provider; live adapters use KEYS-001 connections and are disabled by default.
Reserve, settle or release platform budget per call; timeouts become outcome_unknown and go to reconciliation.
Exclude providers in restricted jurisdictions at configuration time.

packages.title: Authorization server: metadata, client registration, PKCE, resource indicators, tokens and consent records
packages.goal: Run the hub authorization server for the MCP surfaces: RFC 9728 and RFC 8414 metadata, Client ID Metadata Documents with SSRF protection, deprecated dynamic registration behind a hub switch, PKCE S256, exact resource indicators, iss in responses, opaque hashed tokens with refresh rotation and reuse detection, revocation and per-client consent records.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/connections: connection, consent, client registration, token (hash only), token family, connection call, confirmation challenge.

Serve /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource for /mcp and /mcp/admin and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; one authorization server entry; S256 only; iss on every response; client_id_metadata_document_supported and the none token endpoint method.

Fetch client metadata documents only through the egress proxy (HTTPS, private and link-local ranges blocked, size and time limits, cache headers); trust policy any HTTPS client or listed clients only.
Authorization endpoint with the first-party login, step-up and the elevated session for staff; consent per client id and redirect URI; CSRF and frame-ancestors none; progressive scopes.

Token endpoint (form-urlencoded) issuing 15-minute opaque access tokens bound to one surface audience, rotating refresh tokens, DPoP when presented; RFC 7009 revocation; revoke-all on password change and recovery.
acceptance: A token for /mcp is refused on /mcp/admin and on the first-party API, and a session cookie never authorizes /mcp (tested).
Reusing a rotated refresh token revokes the family and suspends the connection (tested).
A metadata document URL resolving to a private address is never fetched (tested).
A changed redirect URI requires new consent.

packages.title: MCP transport and protocol layer

steps: Pin the protocol revisions and the SDK (written reason in the pull request); POST-only endpoint, 405 on GET and DELETE, never mint session ids.
Validate Origin, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name and Mcp-Param headers against the body; answer UnsupportedProtocolVersion with the supported list.
Resolve the bearer token to its connection on every request; check audience, status, kill switches (node, hub, external_agent_api, module, person stop, connection) and toolsets.
Token buckets per connection and class with Retry-After; circuit breaker on repeated denials, loops or injection signatures.
Write a connection_call row per call (argument digest only) and a trace span from the _meta trace context; treat a closed response stream as cancellation.
acceptance: Header and body mismatches answer 400 HeaderMismatch (-32020) (tested).
An engaged kill switch blocks the next call on every surface (tested).
tools/list is deterministic and carries ttlMs and cacheScope.

acceptance: No result contains budgetRange, constraint records, floors, tokenHash or argsDigest without the matching class (forbidden-field scan).

A confirmation opened by another account changes nothing (tested).
An unknown outcome goes to reconciliation and is never retried blindly.

packages.goal: A sourced Australia pack, modelled on the United States pack (INTL-US), so a hub in Australia is configured with data and settings, never with code. The facts listed below are leads to confirm, not pack facts.
steps: Regions and formats: 6 states and the mainland territories (ISO 3166-2:AU); several IANA time zones including half-hour offsets and daylight saving only in some states; four-digit postcodes; phone +61; AUD.
Companies and identifiers: ABN from the Australian Business Register and ACN from ASIC; entity forms (proprietary limited company, public company, sole trader, partnership, trust).

Facets to source: construction licensing (state and territory builder and trade licensing, for example NSW Fair Trading and the Queensland Building and Construction Commission); building codes (National Construction Code by the Australian Building Codes Board, Australian Standards); public procurement (AusTender and state portals); tax (GST, the taxable payments annual report for building and construction, Peppol e-invoicing); e-signatures (Electronic Transactions Act 1999 and state equivalents); payment rails (New Payments Platform with PayID and PayTo, BPAY, cards) and security-of-payment laws per state; privacy (Privacy Act 1988, the Australian Privacy Principles and the OAIC); holidays (national and state public holidays); units (metric).
Languages: en (en-AU).

Every fact with an official primary source, retrieval date and verification level; facts found only in secondary sources stay labelled pending; candidate verification adapters are named as candidates only (no live register call); agent-law defaults stay unverified until counsel review (HUB-005).
acceptance: The pack validates under the v2 schema; every fact cites an official source or is labelled with its lower verification level.
A visitor with country AU sees en-AU formats, AUD and the states and territories.
No engine code branches on AU; no Russian provider or payment rail appears in the pack.

packages.title: Approval routes, decisions and delegation
packages.goal: Let each company configure versioned approval routes per subject kind with built-in segregation of duties, bind every approval to the exact subject digest and keep approvals human.

CSV and XLSX import against a published template creating drafts only, with row-level errors.

Changing a submitted requisition creates a new version and supersedes approvals (test).
Requisitions are visible only to the requester, approvers and members with project scope (negative tests).
External orders produce no reputation records (test).

packages.title: Company supplier base and external counterparties

steps: Migrations for supplier_record, external_counterparty and supplier_assessment.
Link records to claimed, verified or sourced companies by reading only their public projection.
Compute supplier cards from the buyer's own agreements, orders, receipts, matches and documents.
Import suppliers from CSV or XLSX as private records only.

An import never creates a directory member, claim or public record (test).
Assessments never enter reputation snapshots (test).

packages.title: Sourcing events: bid levelling, award decisions and outcome notices

Read prequalification passport sections shared by consent (PREQ-001) as eligibility evidence where available; unknown stays unknown.

Supplier invitation order is identical with and without paid entitlements (comparison test).

packages.title: AI document intake with confidence and human review

Human review queue: accepted reviews create drafts only; meter document pages.
acceptance: No intake path creates an approved, ordered or paid record (test).
Text in a document never changes a payee, sends a message or calls a tool (injection suite).
Every extracted field carries confidence and locator (contract test); egress refused for disallowed data classes (test).

packages.title: Equivalence rules, approved equals and substitutions
packages.goal: Compare equivalent materials through sourced equivalence rules on plan-step terms and product attributes, and decide substitutions only through people (the designer of record where named).

Match lines as equivalent only by a rule that cites its basis; keep equivalent distinct from approved.
Route substitution requests through the approval route kind substitution; keep approved equals with scope and expiry.
acceptance: No agent or rule approves a substitution (test).
A rule without a basis citation cannot be activated (test).
Conversions without a source stay unconverted and flagged (test).

packages.title: Project budgets and cost control
packages.goal: Show planned, committed, actual, forecast and paid per cost code under each project transaction budget, warn before overruns and route budget changes through approvals.

Post commitments from accepted orders, call-offs and external orders, releases at order close, actuals from approved trade invoices, idempotently per source.
Warnings at configurable thresholds as decisions waiting; keep the atomic reservation as the hard stop.
acceptance: Cost entries are idempotent per source and balance against their sources (tests).
Budgets and cost codes never reach suppliers, invited experts or staff without a case grant (negative tests).
A budget increase applies only after approval (test).

packages.title: Goods receipts, dispatch notices, discrepancies and offline capture
packages.goal: Record what arrives at a site or warehouse against orders, partial and offline, with photos, typed discrepancies, supplier notices and returns, separate from quality acceptance.
steps: Migrations for dispatch_notice, goods_receipt, goods_receipt_line and supplier_return.
Offline sync API with client ids, device and server times and idempotent replay.
Order-line balance view (ordered, dispatched, received, accepted, invoiced, returned, open); optional acceptance_record creation for delivery claims.
Discrepancy notices to platform suppliers and drafted messages for external ones.
acceptance: A replayed offline receipt never duplicates (test).
Photo location and faces never appear outside the buyer and that supplier (test).
A receipt never counts as confirmed acceptance unless a person records it (test).

packages.title: Site stock, movements and transfers

Compute balances per item and location; corrections append.
Reorder points propose requisition drafts only.

Stock locations in a restricted place are refused (test).

packages.title: Trade invoices, three-way match and duplicate detection

Supplier-visible status (received, in review, approved, scheduled, paid, disputed) without internal approvers or notes.

Match results and approval records never reach the issuer (forbidden-field tests).

packages.title: Review integrity controls and the public review policy

steps: Validate review eligibility against recorded agreements, tasks or consultations; label and exclude unconfirmed reviews from aggregates.
Detect spikes, rings and reciprocal patterns and open moderation cases; never apply automatic sanctions or silent score changes.
Record every integrity step (checks, cases, decisions) in an append-only log exportable to the hub for regulators.
Publish the review policy page in every hub language from versioned hub text.
acceptance: A review without a recorded relationship is rejected (negative test).
No code path offers an incentive for a review or filters review requests by expected sentiment (test).
A fair negative review cannot be hidden by the reviewed party or by payment; responses and disputes are the only paths.
The policy page renders in every engine language with its version and date.

packages.title: Ranking statements generated from configuration for every ranked surface
packages.goal: Publish, for every ranked surface (directory, matching, needs board, search, recommendations, event listings), the main ranking parameters and the statement that payment has no influence, generated from the active method versions and hub configuration so it can never drift.
steps: Define a ranking-statement contract per surface derived from match, recommendation and search method versions.
Render the public statements page in every hub language and link it from each ranked list.
Regenerate statements on every method or configuration activation and keep the history.
acceptance: Changing a method version changes the published statement in the same activation (test).
Every ranked surface links to its statement; the statement says that payment, plans and sponsorship do not influence ranking, and tests prove it.
The page renders in every engine language.

packages.title: Named-performer confirmation on offers, quotes and work records
packages.goal: Stop identity borrowing: when an offer, quote or work record names a licensed or certified person, that person confirms it from their own account; until then the name shows as not confirmed.
steps: Add a named-performer reference to offer, quote and work-record versions with a confirmation request to the named person.
Show "named performer confirmed" or "not confirmed" in every projection that shows the name; never upgrade a licence badge from the name alone.
Let country packs mark categories where confirmation is required before acceptance.
acceptance: A named person who did not confirm is shown as not confirmed everywhere (projection test).
Only the named person's own account can confirm (negative test with another member of the same company).
Withdrawn confirmation after acceptance is recorded and shown to the counterparty without changing the accepted version.

packages.title: Badge and label vocabulary guard
packages.goal: Prevent misleading trust wording: badge and label texts in every locale use a fixed, counsel-reviewed vocabulary, and the words certified, licensed, guaranteed and approved (and their translations) appear only in keys bound to a register fact or a recorded accreditation.
steps: List the restricted words per engine language and the locale keys allowed to use them.
Add a check that scans locale namespaces and fails on restricted words outside allowed keys.
Document the vocabulary for translators and hub operators.
acceptance: The check fails on a restricted word in an unapproved key in any engine language (test with fixtures).
Allowed keys are tied to sourced or accredited facts in their component contracts.
Adding a language without its restricted-word list fails the check.

packages.title: Worker credential card: holder-presented, offline-verifiable credentials
packages.goal: Give workers a credential card on their phone (identity check level, trainings, licences) that a site, an event or a client verifies offline against the issuing node's key and status list, without the engine ever logging verifications as attendance or location.
steps: Package selected passport credentials into a QR presentation with short validity and selective disclosure where the format supports it.
Provide an offline verifier page that checks signatures and a cached status list.
Show the holder exactly what a verifier sees before presenting.
acceptance: Verification works offline with a status list fetched within its validity (test).
The engine stores no record of who verified whose card, where or when (negative test on audit and logs).
A revoked credential fails verification after the next status list refresh.

packages.title: EU trader traceability for consumer-facing offers
packages.goal: In EU hubs, collect and make best efforts to verify trader traceability information before a trader can offer to consumers, show trader or non-trader status on offers, and let traders meet their information duties (Digital Services Act Articles 30 and 31).
steps: Add traceability fields and verification states from the EU layer of the country packs.
Block consumer-facing offers of traders without complete traceability; show trader status on offers.
Provide a suspension and notice path when information proves inaccurate.
acceptance: A trader without complete traceability cannot publish a consumer-facing offer in an EU hub (test).
Non-EU hubs are unaffected unless their pack enables the facet.
Trader status shows on every consumer-facing offer projection.

packages.title: Wallet-based identity and attribute verification
packages.goal: Let people prove identity and professional attributes with digital identity wallets (EU Digital Identity Wallet, mobile driver's licences, national eID where a hub enables them) through an adapter with a fake, storing verification results and claims, never raw credentials.
steps: Define the verification-level contract (email_verified, document_checked, wallet_verified, in_person) with issuer and date.
Add a relying-party adapter port with a deterministic fake and per-country configuration from packs.
Record results as evidence usable by claims and credentials; show categories, never documents.
acceptance: No raw credential or document is stored (test).
A wallet presentation from a restricted place is refused.
Verification results appear in projections only as categories and dates.

packages.title: Tender source adapters, Open Contracting first
packages.goal: Import public tenders and awards from national portals (SAM.gov, the UK Central Digital Platform, TED, Brazil's PNCP, Chile's Mercado Publico, India's GeM and others) through adapters that map to the Open Contracting Data Standard, each with licence flags and a fake.
steps: Define an OCDS-based mapping contract for notices and awards.
Add adapters with fakes and recorded fixtures per portal family; register each as a source with licence flags.
Feed notices to the opportunities board and awards to sourced track records.
acceptance: No adapter submits bids or contacts buyers (test).
A portal whose terms forbid reuse cannot be activated as a source.
Imported notices are labelled from a public source and never appear as platform members' needs.

packages.title: Electronic signature adapters bound to agreement digests
packages.goal: Let parties sign agreements, acts and waivers with electronic signatures valid in their jurisdiction (ESIGN and UETA providers in the US, eIDAS advanced and qualified signatures in the EU, national schemes elsewhere) through adapters with fakes; the signed document's hash binds to the agreement digest.
steps: Define the signature request and evidence contracts with signature level and provider reference.
Add an adapter port with a deterministic fake; per-country signature levels come from packs.
Reconcile unknown provider outcomes; never resend blindly.
acceptance: A signature over a document whose hash differs from the agreement digest is rejected (test).
Signature levels shown match the pack facts for the parties' jurisdictions.
Unknown outcomes go to reconciliation (fault-injection test).

packages.title: Open BIM exchange for product data and plan items (IFC property sets)
packages.goal: Export and import product entries and plan items as IFC property sets so designers can use Trustwork product data in their BIM tools, without shipping proprietary formats.
steps: Map product entry and plan-step attributes to IFC property sets with the taxonomy crosswalk slots.
Add export and import endpoints with validation and provenance per field.
Document the mapping and its limits.
acceptance: Exports validate against the pinned IFC schema version (test).
Imports never overwrite sourced or claimed facts without provenance.
No proprietary classification ships in the repository.

packages.title: Installable, offline-first mobile web shell
packages.goal: Make the web app installable and dependable on site: manifest and offline shell, encrypted offline caches cleared on sign-out, low-data and sunlight-readable modes, and web push only with permission per category.
steps: Add the web app manifest and an offline shell that never caches other people's data.
Add low-data and high-contrast large-target preferences in every engine language.
Add web push with per-category permission and quiet hours.
acceptance: Signing out or losing access clears offline caches at the next sync (test).
The shell works offline for assigned items only (browser test).
Push is never sent without permission for that category.

packages.title: Accessibility programme: manual audits and a per-hub accessibility statement
packages.goal: Turn WCAG 2.2 AA from a target into recorded evidence: manual walkthroughs per release with screen readers, keyboard, zoom and reduced motion, and an accessibility statement per hub generated from that evidence with a barrier-report contact.
steps: Define the audit record (device, assistive technology, steps, evidence, issues, reviewer) and a release checklist.
Generate the hub accessibility statement page from recorded evidence in every hub language.
Add the brand-overlay contrast check as a launch gate input.
acceptance: The statement never claims conformance beyond recorded evidence (test on generator).
A release without a manual audit record is flagged in the release checklist.
The statement page renders in every engine language.

packages.title: Privacy-preserving analytics: own metrics, cohorts and aggregate readership
packages.goal: Give participants their own metrics and hubs cohort analytics without surveillance: first-party aggregate events with short raw retention, cohorts of at least ten, no third-party trackers, honoured opt-outs and Global Privacy Control.
steps: Define event and cohort contracts with suppression below the minimum cohort.
Aggregate in the worker; expire raw events quickly; expose own metrics to participants and cohorts to hub staff.
Honour opt-outs and Global Privacy Control where the law requires.
acceptance: No per-person behaviour view exists for staff (negative test).
Every count under ten is suppressed (test).
No third-party tracker or advertising identifier is loaded by any page (browser test).

packages.title: Data-broker readiness and deletion-platform adapters
packages.goal: Before a hub enables people data from sources, check whether it may be a data broker under applicable law, record registrations, and process state deletion platforms (for example California's DROP) through an adapter with a fake.
steps: Add a broker-status checklist that gates people datasets in the console.
Add a deletion-platform adapter port with a fake and scheduled retrieval within the legal cadence.
Apply deletions through privacy operations with the erasure ledger and tombstones.
acceptance: A people dataset cannot be activated without a recorded broker-status decision (test).
Deletion requests retrieved from the platform are applied and reported within the configured cadence (clock test).
Deletions propagate to indexes and peers as tombstones.

packages.title: Financing partner referrals: licensed, labelled, never ranking
packages.goal: Let a hub list licensed trade-credit and project-finance partners with disclosed referral fees, shown as labelled options to participants who ask, never influencing ranking, matching, recommendations or reputation, and never consumer lending unless the partner is licensed for it.
steps: Add financing partner records with licence evidence, jurisdictions, products and referral-fee disclosure.
Show partners only on request or in a labelled panel; never in candidate lists.
Screen partners with the compliance package before activation (second person).
acceptance: Rankings are identical with and without financing partners configured (comparison test).
A partner without recorded licence evidence for the jurisdiction cannot be activated.
Referral fees are shown before any referral.
